method: Goal-driven role-play through local actual APIs, continuing after wrong answers to measure recovery instead of stopping at the first failed assertion.
rules: Eight distinct customer goals per area, with 6–10 actual customer turns per journey where possible.
Customer role-play may rephrase, correct details or choose an offered button; bot replies must come from the actual isolated API.
A semantic failure is recorded and does not stop subsequent customer turns or recovery attempts.
Do not force hidden application state to reach a desired branch.
Record checks independently from the final outcome: a customer may eventually obtain help after earlier mistakes.
A correct proposed confirmation or truthful human-support next step can satisfy a goal; no real purchase, diagnosis, claim approval or notification delivery is implied.
Record first misunderstanding and unsuccessful recovery attempts, not just final successful replies.
Actual model calls, remote server performance and live external integrations remain unmeasured.
Keep application code unchanged and preserve all turns; do not weaken the customer goal to obtain a passing result.
No universal 100-point score is inferred from this selected set of synthetic journeys.
